s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, slowly progressive lump with associated pain and discomfort at the posterior aspect of the knee joint
salient_findings: A 3-year history of a lump on the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
Pain and discomfort while walking or standing with the knee joint extended
A 3 x 3 cm sized palpable lump at the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
key_facts: The patient is a 53-year-old woman
The patient has no underlying diseases
The lump is located at the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
The patient experiences pain and discomfort while walking or standing with the knee joint extended
The range of right knee motion is 10-130°
There is no internal swelling of the knee joint
There is no tenderness of the medial or lateral joint line
The Lachman test results are normal
The valgus and varus stress tests are normal
A 3 x 3 cm sized palpable lump is present at the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
Radiographic findings show normal knee joint and lower limb alignments
Mild osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1) is present in both knee joints
MRI findings show a multi-lobulated cyst measuring 3.3 cm × 3.0 cm × 3.9 cm at the popliteal fossa

shortlist.label: Baker's cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-lobulated cyst at popliteal fossa, consistent with Baker's cyst

shortlist.label: Popliteal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst located at posterior aspect of knee joint, consistent with popliteal cyst

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable lump at posterior aspect of knee joint, possible ganglion cyst

raw.rationale: The presence of a multi-lobulated cyst at the popliteal fossa, located next to the posterior aspect of the popliteal artery, is consistent with a Baker's cyst, which is a type of cyst that occurs in the popliteal fossa.

rejected.label: Popliteal cyst
rejected.why: While the location is consistent, 'popliteal cyst' is a more general term and 'Baker's cyst' is a specific diagnosis that better explains the key facts.

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically smaller and more superficial, and are not usually associated with the popliteal fossa.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by synovial inflammation and pigmentation, which is not mentioned in the key facts.

rejected.label: Synovial chondromatosis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by cartilaginous nodules in the synovium, which is not consistent with the MRI findings of a multi-lobulated cyst.
